ramlala.tek: Perform the āratī of Śrī Rāmalalā, the child Rāma, perfect and skilled in the art of archery.
ramlala.cau1: Bow and arrows look beautiful in his hands; before his beauty the pride of millions of Kāmadevas fades.
ramlala.cau2: He is seated on a splendid throne, and at his left shines Vaidehī (Sītā).
ramlala.cau3: Śatrughna and Hanumān stand with folded hands; Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa serve him in many ways.
ramlala.cau4: Śiva, Brahmā and Nārada sing his many virtues; the Vedas say "not this, not this" and find no end to them.
ramlala.cau5: The whole world knows the power of his name; Śeṣa, Maheśa and Gaṇeśa praise it.
ramlala.cau6: He is the wish-granting tree of his devotees, himself wanting nothing, the home of compassion, forgiveness, mercy and every virtue.
ramlala.cau7: He made even Sugrīva king of the monkeys, and the Lord gave Vibhīṣaṇa a kingdom.
ramlala.cau8: As if in play he had the ocean bridged; his matchless fame spread over all the worlds.
ramlala.cau9: He slew the lord of Laṅkā, the fortress none could reach, and took away the fear of gods, men and sages.
ramlala.cau10: He set the gods back in their places, spread his fair fame, and raised up millions of the poor and fallen.
ramlala.cau11: Monkeys, the boatman, the bird (Jaṭāyu) and a demon (Vibhīṣaṇa): in his compassion he took away their sorrows and faults.
ramlala.cau12: He always honours his servants, so the monkey Hanumān became worshipped by the world.
ramlala.cau13: He always honoured the suffering and the lowly; all three worlds ring with "Victory to Rāma".
ramlala.cau14: Kausalyā and all the mothers, Daśaratha and all the Lord's devotees,
ramlala.cau15: gods, men and sages sing the Lord's virtues and find great joy in performing his āratī.
ramlala.cau16: With incense, lamp, sandal paste and food offered, and with a steady mind that keeps no division, (perform the āratī).
ramlala.cau17: Whoever sings the āratī of Rāmalalā gains, by Rāma's grace, the fruit he longs for.
